title: Dark Chocolate Fruit and Nut Mendiants
summary: Glossy discs of tempered dark chocolate topped with dried apricot, cranberries, pistachios and almonds.
equipment: heatproof bowl and pan of barely simmering water

ingredients.note: check the label; many contain soya lecithin or traces of milk

ingredients.item: soft dried apricots, cut into small strips

steps.title: Set out the toppings
steps.text: Line the trays with baking paper and set out the apricot strips, cranberries, pistachios and almonds in small piles so you can work quickly.

steps.title: Melt the chocolate
steps.text: Put two thirds of the chocolate in the bowl over barely simmering water, making sure the bowl does not touch the water. Stir until melted and it reads 45-50 °C.

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Lift the bowl off the pan and add the remaining chocolate. Stir until it has all melted and the chocolate has cooled to 31-32 °C.

steps.title: Test
steps.text: Dip the tip of a knife in the chocolate and leave it at cool room temperature. If it sets glossy and firm within 5 min, it is tempered.

steps.title: Spoon the discs
steps.text: Spoon the chocolate onto the paper in rounds about 5 cm across, working in batches of 6 so they do not set before you top them.

steps.title: Add the toppings
steps.text: While each batch is still wet, press on a strip of apricot, one or two cranberries, a pistachio and an almond.

steps.title: Let them set
steps.text: Leave at cool room temperature for about 30 min, until firm and glossy, then peel the mendiants off the paper.

tips: The most common mistake is overheating the chocolate; above 50 °C it can turn thick and grainy, so melt it gently.
If the test smear stays soft or streaky, add a few more pieces of chopped chocolate and stir until it cools a little more.
Avoid the fridge, which can make the chocolate dull and streaky.
Swap in hazelnuts or candied peel for variety.
storage: Keep in an airtight container at cool room temperature, away from sunlight, for up to 3 weeks.
